gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-huninn: Stomping, adventurous letters stride out wide in Eight Bit Dragon, while Huninn follows in a true monoline, its s terminals kept clear of the body. Contrast in line thickness is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-inter-tig: Inter Tight reads like lines drawn with a technical pen, short ascenders tucked low and curve tails held back from the body. Eight Bit Dragon adds thick-and-thin swagger above it.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-karla: Big, brash and a little stocky, Eight Bit Dragon strides across the line with a towering lowercase, and Karla matches that height with a gaping c. Expect a lively, approachable read.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-kedebider: Kedebideri reads friendly and skyward, its rounded letters staying open and inviting with a tall x-height. Eight Bit Dragon stands over it with a mild stroke contrast, and the two feel like a bold storyteller beside a gentle listener.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-khula: Widely spaced, tall-lowercase letters give Eight Bit Dragon its adventurous stride, with hairlines only slightly lighter than the stems. And Khula, with its squat brush-pen belly and open curves, makes the strongest part of the pair: a steady, modern counterweight.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-krub: Krub reads in a plain sans with a pronounced x-height and pen-lifted curves that leave loops unfinished. And Eight Bit Dragon, with its modest stroke modulation and wide-striding capitals, gives the page a bold headline voice above it.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-kufam: Neon-tube lines meet etched glass here. Kufam keeps one track width throughout, its e generously open, so a long passage would run smooth and contemporary beneath Eight Bit Dragon's subtle weight changes.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-lexend: Lexend comes in with outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve. Over a longer passage it would feel steady and approachable, never tiring, while Eight Bit Dragon sets the adventurous tone above it with a measured weight difference like thread against yarn.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-lexend-de: Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded line, with terminals that stop short of curling back and capitals that look small beside its big lowercase. Lexend Deca against the stencil-cut Eight Bit Dragon makes the pair's clearest quality: bold shapes over a quiet sans-serif.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-liter: Liter reads as a constant-width line, like a marker, with tall lowercase and wide mouths. Eight Bit Dragon keeps real weight even in its thinnest curves, so the two feel bold above and steady below, in sans-serif and display form.
